theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorWantedHeader.meets {pMain free h J len : ℕ} {μ : ℕ → ℤ}
    (main : P[pMain]?=some _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorWantedHeader.body) (hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word)
    (hspace : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightGuardedWanted.wantedFree free h J len ≤ lim.space)
    (H : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightCoverKeyData.Stored μ free h J) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim P pMain d [free,J,len] μ (_root_.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorWantedHeader.time J)
      (fun r ν => r=(_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightGuardedWanted.wantedFree free h J len : ℤ) ∧ ν=μ) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,h,J,\ell\in\mathbb N$ be cover base, microblock parameter, block count and A-incidence length. Suppose memory $\mu$ satisfies the complete retained cover/key-data contract at $f$. For Light limits, program and depth $\lambda,P,d$, assume the program contains the wanted-header body, addresses fit words and the computed wanted-header address fits memory. Then the call on $(f,J,\ell)$ returns

$$\operatorname{wantedFree}(f,h,J,\ell),$$

within its prescribed $J$-dependent time, leaving all memory unchanged.

This obtains the next physical header from retained construction data rather than external pointer advice.
